records.title: Safe-suite and destructive-flash runtime results were reported separately
records.content: The archived session reported a historical safe-suite run of 20 tests: 12 PASS, 3 FAIL, and 5 INFO, with screen values independently checked against raw emulator memory. For the opt-in destructive suite, TD4 passed at runtime, TD5 reports INFO and TD6 SKIP by design, while TD1-TD3 remained unconfirmed at runtime because available emulators did not implement the required flash-write behavior correctly. These are historical results, not current-build claims.
evidence: GBE+ and mGBA validation discussed in archived session

records.title: Flash buffer commit uses literal zero and reset is issued once
records.content: The implementation discussion corrected two flash command details after cross-checking shonumi/dandocs, FlashGBX, and sanni/cartreader: the buffered-program commit is a distinct write of literal $00, not a repeated data byte, and the reset command $F0 is issued once per window. The session also applied the confirmed $1000/$0C00 flash enable sequence before destructive operations. Preserve the cited source distinctions and do not infer current implementation state without checking code.

records.title: Real cartridge photos confirmed the Macronix flash part
records.content: The owner supplied Game Boy hardware database photos of two physical MBC6 cartridges. The session reported that both showed the Macronix MX29F008TC-14 flash chip, independently corroborating the project's existing target. The same photos showed a Mitsumi MM1134A supervisor/reset component; its relationship, if any, to MBC6 write protection or register $1000 was explicitly left unknown and was not made normative behavior.

records.title: Mitsumi MM1134A role in MBC6 flash write protection is unresolved
records.content: Photos of two MBC6 cartridges show a Mitsumi MM1134A supervisor/reset component. The archived session found no source proving whether it interacts with MBC6 registers such as $1000 or is only part of independent power/reset protection. Keep this as an explicit unknown; do not encode a software behavior assumption without further hardware evidence.

records.title: Explain every on-screen test status and distinguish tests absent from a build
records.content: The project owner asked what the screen status letters mean. The screen guide defines P as PASS, F as FAIL, S as SKIP, I as INFO, and a dash as not run in this build. Preserve this user-facing explanation and distinguish a test that was not compiled into a build from one that passed.
